items.summary: Luxury brands like Hermes and Cartier face steeper slumps in mainland China as wealthy consumers reduce spending. Sales for major labels fell by double digits in August and September, according to research firms. While resilient demand in Hong Kong and Macau offset some mainland declines, earnings remain weighed down. Executives fear the slump could persist until 2027 due to scrutiny of offshore wealth and a cooling AI stock rally. Consumers are shifting toward experiences and understated products, signaling a structural problem rather than a temporary dip.
items.title: Wealthy Chinese Consumers Cut Back on Luxury Spending

items.summary: Singapore Exchange CEO Loh Boon Chye announced he will step down in 2027. He cited the bourse's strong performance and foundation as the opportunity to plan a thoughtful leadership transition. Chairman Koh Boon Hwee described the decision as bittersweet, crediting Loh with stabilizing the company and transforming it into a global multi-asset platform.
items.title: SGX CEO Loh Boon Chye to step down in 2027

items.summary: An article originally published on the Vanishing Gradients Substack outlines a framework for agentic software factories, designed to allow autonomous and asynchronous execution of software tasks. The authors propose a four-layer hierarchy: harness, personalization, automation, and continual learning. This structure enables agents to build and operate software independently, reducing the need for constant human oversight. The framework emphasizes specification and verification to ensure reliability. Examples include an invoice tracker and a media business setup, demonstrating how agents can handle repetitive tasks, perform checks, and improve over time without retraining. The authors argue this approach empowers non-engineers to direct software development by delegating implementation while retaining control over decisions and trade-offs.
items.title: Authors Propose Agentic Software Factory Hierarchy of Needs

items.summary: The nuclear industry faces a critical leadership challenge as it prepares for a projected four million professionals by 2050. Success depends not just on technical skills but on leaders who can navigate complex international systems, manage diverse supply chains, and foster safety cultures. The World Nuclear University Summer Institute addresses this by training mid-career professionals in global contexts, such as the 2027 program in Cape Town. With over 1,700 alumni from 90 countries, the initiative builds networks essential for managing new builds and extending existing fleets. Applications for the 2027 cohort close on 27 November 2026.
items.title: Nuclear Industry Leaders Need Global Skills for Future Growth

items.summary: Greece's renewable electricity capacity is approaching 20 GW, driven by significant additions in wind and photovoltaic projects. Despite high curtailments and low wholesale prices impacting profitability, the sector continues to expand. The Independent Power Transmission Operator expects installations to reach nearly 20 GW by year-end, while the Ministry of Environment and Energy aims for 4 GW of storage by 2028. Industry groups highlight concerns over market distortions and investment delays.
items.title: Greece Renewable Capacity Growth Amid Market Challenges

items.summary: Infosys Ltd reported a 6.23 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 7,823 crore for the second quarter of FY27. Revenue from operations rose 10.7 per cent to Rs 49,244 crore. In constant currency terms, revenue grew 1.5 per cent year-on-year and 1.2 per cent quarter-on-quarter.
items.title: Infosys Reports Profit Rise and Revenue Growth in Q2 FY27

items.summary: Tata Motors Ltd reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 1,257 crore for Q2 FY27, a 50.90% decline from Q1 but a recovery from a loss last year. Revenue rose 36%, though the headline profit was impacted by lower mark-to-market losses on Tata Capital investments.
items.title: Tata Motors Reports Q2 Net Profit Amid Revenue Growth

items.summary: Infosys reduced its fiscal year 2027 revenue growth forecast to 1-2 percent, down from 1.5-3 percent, despite beating quarterly estimates. The company cited increased demand from energy and utility clients. However, the broader IT sector faces headwinds from AI, which is shifting client focus toward productivity gains rather than traditional billing models. Infosys shares remained flat ahead of results.
items.title: Infosys Lowers Revenue Growth Forecast Amid AI Industry Challenges

items.summary: A former Justice Department official told Semafor that a Tesla-SpaceX merger could face real antitrust risks due to potential vertical foreclosure. Sen. Cory Booker stated that if Elon Musk proceeds, the deal would carry risks for global antitrust enforcers. Additionally, Reuters reported that Tesla's work in China and its relationship with the Pentagon could complicate matters, while Democrats might scrutinize the deal if they regain control of the House.
items.title: Elon Musk's Potential Tesla-SpaceX Merger Faces Antitrust Scrutiny

items.summary: This week's VoxDev newsletter highlights diverse development economics research. Topics include a new framework for scaling education interventions, GPS apps reshaping tractor rental markets in Kenya, and job search mismatches in Addis Ababa. Studies also examine tax collection efficiency, showing low-income countries collect significantly less per dollar spent than high-income nations, and find no gender discrimination in Ethiopian loan decisions.
items.title: VoxDev Weekly Highlights Research on Education, Agriculture, and Tax Efficiency

items.summary: Jensen Huang stated there is a scarcity of capital for the AI buildout, noting demand exceeds availability. This comment follows a selloff where S&P 500 futures fell 0.28% and the Nasdaq dropped 2.6%. CoreWeave stock declined 10%, while Nvidia and Alphabet shares also fell. CNBC reports the selloff highlights worries that financing, rather than demand, could limit the AI rally.
items.title: Jensen Huang warns of AI capital scarcity amid market drops

items.summary: Facing prohibitive new car prices averaging over $50,000 and monthly payments exceeding $765, many young Americans are increasingly purchasing older Y2K-era vehicles. Jack Price, a Marine veteran, exemplifies this trend by driving a 2010 Volkswagen Jetta he bought for $6,000, noting the financial relief of avoiding a car payment. While experts like Keith Barry caution that older cars may lack modern safety features and suffer from reliability issues, buyers cite the ability to perform DIY repairs and the lower total cost of ownership as primary attractions. Despite the shrinking inventory of affordable used vehicles, the movement persists as a response to economic strain, with some owners embracing the mechanical challenges as part of the vehicle's appeal.
items.title: Young Americans Turn to Y2K Cars Amidst Rising Vehicle Costs

items.summary: South Africa has proposed a new fiscal law designed to protect public finances from future populist governments, coinciding with a projected decline in debt for the first time in nearly two decades. Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana introduced the measure to lock in gains, noting that debt stabilized at around $366 billion, or 78% of GDP, after rising from 24% in 2009. Unlike other nations, the draft law lacks a specific numerical ceiling, instead requiring future administrations to explain deviations from their announced plans. While economists view the numbers as warranting a credit rating upgrade, critics argue the approach relies on an optimistic premise that political explanations will suffice to maintain fiscal discipline.
items.title: South Africa Proposes New Fiscal Law to Shield Public Finances

items.summary: A new study analyzed over one million resolved contracts across four platforms, including Polymarket and Kalshi, covering twelve domains. The research found that forecast probabilities were highly calibrated, with events occurring approximately as predicted. While systematic tendencies toward over- or underestimation exist in highly consequential areas, large-scale aggregation of judgments provides meaningful information about real-world uncertainty.
items.title: New Analysis Confirms High Accuracy of Prediction Markets Across Diverse Domains

items.summary: Max Doppelt flew to Shanghai to obtain a lung cancer drug approved in China but not the US, noting his mother has survived three years on it. He reports at least 30 Americans have made similar trips. Doppelt argues this highlights a need for FDA reform, citing a proposal by Reps. John Moolenaar and Debbie Dingell to require Treasury clearance for pharmaceutical deals with Chinese companies.
items.title: Max Doppelt Urges FDA Reform After Flying to China for Cancer Drug

items.summary: Global equity funds attracted $28.16 billion in net inflows during the week through October 21, marking a fifth consecutive week of positive capital flow. LSEG Lipper data attributes this trend to easing Treasury yields and strong corporate earnings, which lifted investor sentiment across Asian, European, and US markets.
items.title: Global Equity Funds See Fifth Consecutive Week of Inflows

items.summary: Meta is introducing fees for posting hyperlinks on Facebook, limiting free posts to two per month while charging $49.99 for eight links and $499 for unlimited access. This move follows similar restrictions on Instagram and X. Meanwhile, Oracle faces scrutiny over its $300 billion deal with OpenAI amid $169 billion in debt, as AI efficiency gains challenge the viability of massive data center investments. Separately, utilities may pass grid upgrade costs to consumers even if speculative data centers are never built, and the Trump administration authorized a release of 315,000 barrels of heating oil reserves to potentially lower prices.
items.title: Meta Charges for Hyperlinks as Tech Giants Face Debt and Data Center Uncertainty

items.summary: The government is expected to raise the earnings limit for its new first-time buyer loan scheme to £110,000 outside London and £140,000 in the capital. These changes, reported by The Times, aim to include middle-earning couples like teachers and nurses. Details are due at next week's Budget.
items.title: Government raises earnings cap for first-time buyer loan scheme

items.summary: Retail sales in Great Britain fell 0.4% month on month in September, steeper than the expected 0.1% drop. The Office for National Statistics reported the decline was driven by poor online clothing sales due to warm weather. Stripping out fuel, sales fell 0.7%. Consumer confidence has fallen at the fastest rate since the pandemic.
items.title: Retail sales in Great Britain fell more steeply than expected last month

items.summary: Xiongan New Area in Hebei Province is developing as a model smart city by integrating digital and physical infrastructure. The Xiongan Urban Computing Center acts as the digital brain, supporting over 100 data categories from 20 government departments. AI applications optimize traffic flow, reducing peak travel times by 15 minutes in Rongdong District, while smart systems monitor utilities and detect safety hazards. The city has built more than 500 kilometers of digital roads and over 130 kilometers of digital utility tunnels. By 2027, Xiongan aims to attract five unicorn companies and 100 leading enterprises to foster innovation and talent development.
items.title: Xiongan New Area Deploys AI and Digital Infrastructure for Smart City Vision

items.summary: China Media Group (CMG) launched a multilingual AI production platform for short dramas and animated series at the International Audio-Visual Arts Gala in Shanghai on October 18. The event, held at the Shanghai Exhibition Center, showcased projects combining technology and art. CMG officials and Shanghai Mayor Zhu Zhongming addressed the gathering, pledging deeper cooperation to support cultural innovation through technology and promote international exchanges.
items.title: China Media Group Launches Multilingual AI Platform at Shanghai Event

items.summary: The 2026 'China Walk: Vibrant Hainan' joint media tour launched in Sanya on October 19, bringing together journalists from 11 outlets across eight ASEAN countries. Hosted by China Media Group and the Hainan Bureau, the event explores rural revitalization and development within the Hainan Free Trade Port through on-site reporting and multimedia content distribution.
items.title: China Walk Media Tour Launches in Hainan for ASEAN Journalists

items.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping recalled the 'Half a Quilt' story during a gathering commemorating the 90th anniversary of the Long March victory. He emphasized that remembering history is crucial for creating a brighter future and stressed the importance of people's support. The article notes that Shazhou Village, where the story originated, has seen significant improvements in livelihoods and income since 2012, reflecting the Party's commitment to modernization and shared prosperity.
items.title: Xi Jinping Recalls 'Half a Quilt' Story at Long March Anniversary

items.summary: Police in a Parisian suburb are treating a shooting as a terrorist incident. French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu stated that one person was killed and at least four others injured in Trappes. The National Anti-Terrorist Prosecutor's Office has taken over the investigation. Reports suggest the number of injured may be higher, potentially including a 12-year-old child. The Mayor of Trappes reported that an individual fired shots from a vehicle at several people.
items.title: One Dead, Four Injured in Paris Suburb Shooting Treated as Terrorist Incident

items.summary: Oil prices reached a five-month high amid fears of renewed US military strikes on Iran. Brent crude rose 1% to $114.72 a barrel. Analysts note that reports of potential attacks, rather than a brief conflict, have driven market volatility. Tensions remain high as Iran threatens retaliation against Gulf facilities and US forces consider action following elections.
items.title: Oil Prices Surge on Fears of Renewed US Strikes on Iran

items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham warned the UK could face a winter of greater flooding. Speaking at a wildfire summit, he emphasized the need for resilience as unexpected events become more common. He also addressed supply preparedness and upcoming storms.
items.title: Andy Burnham Warns UK Faces Winter Flooding Risks Amid Climate Concerns

items.summary: Doctors told the BBC that paramilitary fighters systematically destroyed el-Fasher's healthcare system during a siege in Darfur a year ago. A BBC investigation found evidence supporting these claims of targeting. UN human rights chief Volker Türk described the findings as deeply disturbing, noting that attacking health facilities is illegal under international law. However, Dr Alaa Eldin Nugud, the health minister of the group's civilian-affiliated government, dismissed the allegations as propaganda.
items.title: Doctors Report Paramilitary Targeting of Sudanese Hospitals in Darfur

items.summary: The Japanese government highlighted the urgent need to strengthen its energy supply-and-demand structure in the fiscal 2025 white paper, adopted at a Cabinet meeting. The document notes Japan was the first to release petroleum reserves due to the Middle East situation. It also outlines plans to secure fossil fuel supplies while accelerating nuclear and renewable energy use.
items.title: Japan Calls for Stronger Energy Supply Structure in Fiscal 2025 White Paper

items.summary: An explosion at a privately owned coal mine in Gelik, Turkey, killed two miners and injured five others, with one person still trapped. Local authorities attributed the blast to firedamp. Zonguldak governor Osman Hacibektasoglu confirmed two deaths after hospitalization. Rescue teams from AFAD and medical crews responded to the site. An investigation has been opened to determine the exact cause of the incident.
items.title: Explosion at Turkish Coal Mine Kills Two, Traps One

items.summary: Military reinforcements are moving to the Middle East as the U.S. and Israel prepare for a possible attack on Iran following the midterm elections, according to a person briefed on war planning. Iran has stated it is prepared for both diplomacy and war, demanding formal control over the Strait of Hormuz and the withdrawal of U.S. troops. Meanwhile, millions of Americans have already voted early, with Democrats voting at higher rates than Republicans in key battleground states, though experts caution against overinterpreting early data as a predictor of final results.
items.title: Military Reinforcements Move to Mideast as U.S. Prepares for Possible Iran Attack

items.summary: French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez held a press conference to announce security arrangements for upcoming protests. He stated that 70,000 security forces would be mobilized on October 24 to maintain order during the events.
items.title: French Interior Minister Announces Security Mobilization for Upcoming Protests

items.summary: Gary Huang Kunjie was sentenced to 28 weeks in jail for filming upskirt videos of women in June 2026. The court warned him he could face caning if he reoffends. Huang admitted to recording around 20 victims between May and June 2026. He has a history of similar convictions from 2018 to 2025. Judge Arvindren expressed concern Huang might continue reoffending despite his remorse.
items.title: Serial voyeur jailed again for upskirt videos in Singapore

items.summary: Two Indigenous women in Brazil were denied interpreter assistance while voting in Macapá, despite their inability to speak Portuguese. Their community leader, Mitore Tiriyó Kaxuyana, reported that poll workers restricted translator access to voters with disabilities only. The women left unsure if their votes were counted correctly. This incident reflects broader concerns about Indigenous voting rights and language access in Brazil's electoral system.
items.title: Indigenous Women Denied Interpreter Assistance During Brazil Election

items.summary: More than four million Latinos have turned 18 since the 2022 midterm elections and will vote for the first time on November 3. This new generation, alongside one million naturalized citizens, brings the total number of new eligible Latino voters to 5.2 million compared to four years ago. Hispanics now account for 16% of all voting-age citizens. The median age of eligible Hispanic voters is 39, significantly younger than other groups. Many new voters cite concerns over immigration policy, ICE operations, and the economy as primary motivations for their participation in the upcoming election.
items.title: Millions of Young Latinos Set to Vote for First Time in Midterms

items.summary: Meghan Markle stated she was informed of disturbing allegations against her father in 2018, leading her to limit his contact with their children. Thomas Markle denied possessing alleged child sexual abuse material found in the Philippines. Meghan cited a 2018 letter to police and expressed hope for justice and child safety.
items.title: Meghan Markle Reveals 2018 Warning About Father's Allegations

items.summary: The Japan Times and News2u Holdings warn partners and former employees that unauthorized access to a server used until August 2022 may have exposed business and personal data, including MyNumber details, though digital services remain unaffected.
items.title: Japan Times and News2u Warn Partners of Potential Data Exposure

items.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu faces a challenging re-election campaign three years after the October 7 Hamas attack, which killed over 1,200 people and took 250 hostages. While Likud holds a parliamentary majority, polls show the party's worst performance since 2006, with support hovering around 19 to 20 seats. Analysts note Netanyahu's weakened position compared to potential winner Gadi Eisenkot, yet he leverages the ongoing conflict and opposition to Arab parties to maintain a realistic chance of power. His strategy involves portraying himself as the only leader capable of finishing the war against Iran, a narrative reinforced by U.S. President Donald Trump.
items.title: Netanyahu Stakes Re-election on War Promise Amid Poll Decline

items.summary: Storm Austen, named by UK forecasters, is sweeping across northwestern France, bringing violent gusts and severe disruption. Approximately 161,000 households in the north-west, including Brittany and Normandy, lost electricity. The storm has triggered orange alerts in 23 departments and caused transport issues due to fallen trees and strong winds reaching 161 km/h.
items.title: Storm Austen Causes Widespread Power Outages and Disruption in France

items.summary: Infosys announced a dividend of Rs 26 per share, payable on November 11 to shareholders holding demat accounts as of November 3. The IT major reported a 6% year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 7,823 crore for the July-September quarter, alongside an 11% increase in revenue from operations to Rs 49,244 crore.
items.title: Infosys Announces Dividend and Reports Strong Q2 Profit Growth

items.summary: Apple launched its foldable iPhone Duo on Friday, reviving scenes of overnight lines and intense demand despite limited supply. The device, priced from $2,000 up to $3,199 for high-storage models, marks a major design shift in the company's nearly two-decade history. While crowds gathered in cities like Beijing and Singapore, many buyers were existing Apple customers eager for innovation. However, production challenges involving advanced hinges and display technology, along with component shortages, have constrained availability. Consequently, new orders face delivery delays extending into late January or even December, marking some of the longest waits for a new Apple product in recent years.
items.title: Apple launches foldable iPhone Duo amid supply shortages and high demand

items.summary: Tata Motors Ltd reported a net profit of ₹2,138 crore in the September quarter, marking a return to standalone profitability after a previous loss. Standalone revenue jumped 41.9% to ₹23,930 crore, driven by higher commercial vehicle volumes. Managing Director Girish Wagh highlighted strong underlying demand and disciplined execution. The company also noted steady progress in its Iveco acquisition, with consolidation expected from the December quarter.
items.title: Tata Motors Reports Profit Rebound and Iveco Acquisition Progress

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to inaugurate the Reserve Bank of India's Rs 169-crore data centre in Jatni, Odisha, on October 25. Officials stated the facility, spanning 18.55 acres, will enhance cybersecurity and disaster recovery. BJP leader Jatin Mohanty noted this marks the PM's ninth visit to the state since 2024, aiming to boost digital infrastructure and electronics manufacturing.
items.title: PM Modi to Inaugure RBI Data Centre in Odisha

items.summary: Infosys reduced its fiscal year 2027 revenue growth forecast to 1-2%, down from 1.5-3%, despite reporting a 10.7% quarterly revenue increase. The company cited AI-driven shifts in client demand and pricing pressures as key factors. While the energy segment grew 7.3%, overall revenue rose only 1.5% excluding currency effects. Net profit increased 6.2% but missed analyst expectations.
items.title: Infosys Lowers FY27 Revenue Growth Forecast Amid AI Challenges

items.summary: Tata Motors Limited announced a consolidated net profit of ₹1,257 crore for the quarter ended 30 September 2026, a substantial increase from ₹530 crore in the previous year. Consolidated revenue from operations rose 36% to ₹25,338 crore, while profit before tax turned positive at ₹1,998 crore after a loss in the prior period. MD & CEO Girish Wagh attributed the growth to broad-based performance across segments.
items.title: Tata Motors Reports Strong Q2 FY27 Earnings and Profit Growth

items.summary: Lionel Messi requested a chess opening tailored to his playing style from the AI chatbot ChatGPT, a video of the interaction that went viral on social media. The AI suggested the opening known as 'Goat Horns,' consisting of the moves 1.e4 a6 2.d4 c6. Chess.com noted that AI models often provide poor chess advice and that top professionals are unlikely to approve this specific opening. The video was captioned by ChatGPT, stating it suggested 'Goat Horns.' This incident occurred shortly after OpenAI released an updated interface for visual and interactive responses.
items.title: Messi Asks ChatGPT for a Chess Opening Matched to His Style

items.summary: Tata Group-owned retailer Westside introduced a fixed Rs 49 fee for all credit card transactions starting October 8, 2026. The company did not specify the reason for the charge, though it noted processing costs like MDR often drive such fees. The Reserve Bank of India has not issued specific instructions on credit card surcharges, distinguishing them from debit card rules. Customers are advised to check bills before payment.
items.title: Westside Introduces Rs 49 Credit Card Fee Amid RBI Silence

items.summary: Microsoft is shutting down The Garage, a 17-year-old program that provided maker spaces and tools for employee side projects across 15 regions. CEO Satya Nadella participated in its hackathons, which produced products like Seeing AI and the Xbox Adaptive Controller. While the program ends, Microsoft states experimentation will continue within daily team workflows, though specific impacts on locations and employees remain unclear.
items.title: Microsoft Closes The Garage Maker Lab Program

items.summary: Tesla announced a financing offer for the Model Y in India on October 23, featuring a monthly payment of Rs 39,990 under a seven-year step-up EMI plan at 8.5% interest. The company claims an effective cost of Rs 19,990 by deducting estimated fuel and maintenance savings, though this figure is not the actual loan instalment. The promotion runs during the Switch and Save Carnival at experience centres across major Indian cities.
items.title: Tesla Launches Model Y Financing Offer in India

items.summary: Raj Thackeray of the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena accused the BJP of murdering democracy, alleging the party used religious polarisation to divert attention from a viral audio clip. Thackeray claimed the recording featured BJP and RSS officials discussing strategies to silence activist Manoj Jarange regarding a Rs 500 crore payment. While Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis ordered a forensic examination, BJP leaders questioned the clip's authenticity and suggested it might be AI-generated.
items.title: Raj Thackeray Accuses BJP of Democracy Murder Over Audio Clip

items.summary: Delhi Police detained protesters attempting to march to the Election Commission headquarters against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. Authorities imposed prohibitory orders banning mass gatherings. The demonstration, organized by the Delhi Coordination Committee of People Against SIR, drew students, youth, and activists. Organizers stated the protest would remain peaceful. Security was tightened in central Delhi with traffic diversions in place.
items.title: Protesters Detained as March Against Electoral Roll Revision Heads to Election Commission

items.summary: A commentary highlights an 81% global decline in migratory freshwater fish since the 1970s, driven by habitat fragmentation and dams. While a 2026 disaster in Nepal demonstrated the fragility of infrastructure and the ecological disruption of sediment floods, the author argues that top-down engineering often fails. Instead, the piece points to successful community-led conservation in Meghalaya, Bhutan, and Nagaland. These grassroots models protect spawning grounds without concrete, offering a viable alternative to restore river biodiversity and support local livelihoods.
items.title: Community Models Offer Hope for Disappearing Migratory Fish

items.summary: Cockroach Janata Party leaders appeared in court regarding bail conditions and trespassing charges. Simultaneously, a strike by 40,000 Haryana electricity workers caused power outages affecting 50,000 households. The Haryana Power Minister opposes privatization and plans to challenge the regulatory commission's order. Leaders face summons from the Delhi Police Crime Branch regarding ongoing investigations.
items.title: Cockroach Janata Party Leaders Face Legal Scrutiny Amid Power Strike

items.summary: Approximately 40,000 Haryana electricity employees launched a three-day strike in Gurugram and Nuh, protesting a regulatory decision to grant a parallel power distribution licence to a private firm. The action triggered massive outages affecting over 50,000 households and 1,800 manufacturing units, causing severe water shortages and business disruptions. The state government opposes privatisation and plans to legally challenge the order.
items.title: Electricity Workers Strike in Haryana Causes Widespread Power Outages

items.summary: Mississippi officials lowered a 31-ton propane tank and steel tower into the Gulf to create an artificial reef. Supported by Chevron and local fire departments, the structures aim to provide shelter for fish in areas with limited natural habitats. While a 2023 reef supported over 530 red snapper, no figures exist yet for this new deployment. The project is expected to benefit both commercial and recreational fishing.
items.title: Mississippi Deploys Retired Firefighting Equipment as Artificial Reef

items.summary: Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu appointed Asian Para Games gold medallist Suvarna Raj as the State Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities. Officials stated she was selected from a panel of three candidates recommended by a committee. Raj, a discus throw champion and disability rights advocate, will oversee safeguards for persons with disabilities under the law.
items.title: Asian Para Games gold medallist Suvarna Raj appointed Delhi disability commissioner

items.summary: Delhi authorities seized over 322 kg of ghee from stores offering steep discounts ahead of the festive season. Inspections targeted retailers promoting deals like 'Buy One, Get One Free' and discounts up to 60 per cent. Officials collected samples from locations including Vikaspuri and Hastal village to assess quality and prevent the sale of adulterated products. Further action will follow laboratory test reports.
items.title: Delhi Seizes Hundreds of Kilograms of Ghee Amidst Discount Checks

items.summary: Delhi Police detained protesters marching against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls on Friday, October 23. Organized by People Against SIR, the demonstration invoked Section 163 of the BNSS to bar mass gatherings. Participants, including leaders from CPI(M) and AIDWA, shouted slogans demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The collective plans further protests in 88 cities across 18 states.
items.title: Delhi Police Detain Protesters During Anti-SIR March

items.summary: Rohini Mokashi-Punekar reviews Luke Kennard's 2026 Booker-shortlisted novel, Black Bag, which explores enforced anonymity through a professor's experiment based on Robert Zajonc's mere-exposure effect. The unnamed narrator, an out-of-work actor, is zipped into a black leather bag and forced to remain characterless. While the novel contrasts this concealment with Claudio's hyper-visibility and critiques Internet commodification, the reviewer finds the plot insubstantial and the middle stodgy. Although the book features striking, disparate moments, it fails to fully examine contemporary anxieties, leaving the reader feeling cheated of an epiphany. The review concludes that the novel suffers from an uninspired close despite its adventurous chase sequence.
items.title: Review of Luke Kennard's Novel Black Bag

items.summary: Kerala Food and Civil Supplies Minister Anoop Jacob urged the Centre to extend the deadline for activating ration cards via e-KYC. He requested flexibility in implementing the 2025 amendment order affecting over 44,000 priority cardholders who have not purchased supplies for six months. Jacob argued that immediate removal could be unjust and proposed retaining cards under a state category until eligibility is reassessed.
items.title: Kerala Minister Urges Centre to Extend Ration Card e-KYC Deadline

items.summary: State Bank of India is notifying customers individually after a suspected cyber incident flagged 3,897 records containing personal data. The bank, which received alerts on October 16, assures that funds remain safe and has appointed an independent agency to investigate. While the exposure is confirmed, the bank states the incident has not impacted core operations or financial performance.
items.title: SBI notifies customers after cyber incident flags 3,897 records

items.summary: The State Bank of India stated on Friday that it notified customers via email or WhatsApp following a cyberattack that leaked approximately 3.75 lakh records, including 3,897 containing personally identifiable information. The bank confirmed account balances remain safe and advised vigilance against suspicious communications. This disclosure followed criticism from the Internet Freedom Foundation regarding the bank's initial failure to notify affected individuals.
items.title: State Bank of India Informs Customers After Cyberattack Data Leak
